chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Mansur al-Sayqal, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Sometimes a man supplicates with a supplication, so it is answered for him, then that is delayed for a while.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' I said, 'And why is that, so that he may increase in supplication?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.
ai.seo_question: Why is a supplication sometimes answered but delayed?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the delay in answering a supplication serves as a divine mechanism to deepen the supplicant's spiritual engagement by encouraging persistent and increased prayer. This concept highlights the value of the act of supplication itself as a means of drawing closer to God, rather than viewing delay merely as a withholding of favor. Such teachings underscore the Shia understanding of divine wisdom in timing, where patience and continued devotion are rewarded with greater spiritual elevation.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ahmad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Mansour Al Sayqal who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Sometimes the man supplicates with the supplication, so it is Answered for him. Then it is delayed for a while’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’. I said, ‘And why would that be so, in order for him to increase from the supplications?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Mansur al-Sayqal who has said the following:

“Once I asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) ‘Is it possible that at one time a man prays and it is accepted and then is delayed for a period of time?’ The narrator has said that the Imam then said, ‘Yes, it can happen.’ I then asked, ‘Why is that? Is it because so he will increase his prayer and pleading?’ The Imam said, ‘Yes, that is right.’”
